Compute the answer yourself; no files, network, or saved state are involved. The grid is a deterministic function of seed, size, and symmetric. Let n be the side length (5, 7, 9, or 11). Use this generator. A Stream has namespace "crossword" and key f"{seed}|{size}|{int(symmetric)}", so for this input the key is "930|11x11|1". Its draws are numbered k=0,1,2,...; draw k is the first 8 bytes, big-endian, of sha256(f"crossword|{key}|{k}".encode()). below(m)=draw%m; between(lo,hi)=lo+below(hi-lo+1); chance(p,q)=below(q)<p; every draw advances k by one. Start with an n x n all-white grid. style=below(10). If style==0, stop: the grid is all white. Otherwise: percent=between(10,28); scan cells in row-major order r=0..n-1, c=0..n-1; if symmetric and r*n+c > (n-1-r)*n+(n-1-c), skip that cell; otherwise, if chance(percent,100) is true, paint (r,c) black and, if symmetric, also paint (n-1-r,n-1-c) black. After the scan, if style==1, draw line=below(n) and paint that whole row black (mirrored if symmetric); if style==2, draw line=below(n) and paint that whole column black (mirrored). Rows are strings of '.' for white and '#' for black.

Now build the runs list: every maximal run of white cells, across and down, single cells included, ordered by first cell (row, then column), and across before down when the first cell is the same. The first cell of an across run is its left end; the first cell of a down run is its top end.

Numbering: a run of length 1 is no entry and gets 0. Scan all cells row-major, top to bottom, left to right; each cell that starts at least one run of length >=2 gets the next clue number, starting at 1. A cell that starts both an across and a down run has one clue number used by both runs. Output one number per run in the runs-list order: the clue number if the run's length is >=2, otherwise 0. Return only that numbers array.
